body: A Nature study combined a meta-analysis of 70 experiments with 32 years of field observations from 533 plots in South Africa’s Kruger National Park. It found that elevated carbon dioxide increased aboveground biomass in wild C4 grasses most clearly under water-limited conditions, challenging the simple assumption that C4 grasses respond only weakly to higher CO₂.

Savannah forecasts depend on competition among grasses, woody plants, water and fire. If rising CO₂ also fertilizes C4 grasses under drought, models that mainly emphasize CO₂-driven woody encroachment may be missing part of the system. The result is a synthesis plus long-term observational evidence, not a forecast that every savannah will become more productive.

It is worth time precisely because so much modern life is evaluated through productivity, optimization and measurable contribution. Zhuangzi’s counterproposal is more radical than work-life balance: sometimes the category of usefulness itself is what distorts our view of what is valuable.
